statement: In the three years after the busway began (October 2019 to September 2022), crashes injuring or killing a pedestrian on 14th Street between Ninth and Third Avenues fell by about a third relative to 23rd, 34th, 42nd and 57th Streets over the same avenues, compared with the five years before.

edge.effect: pedestrian injury crashes on the corridor

graph_evidence.concepts: pedestrian injury, traffic volume, bus lane
graph_evidence.summary: The graph has many pedestrian-injury variables but none for a bus-only street or volume reduction; the nearest is Lima, where crossings at bus stops on bus-only lanes had more pedestrian collisions, OR 2.36 (1.02-5.42) (PMID 24357516, abstract read). Busways concentrate buses and bus stops, which this finding links to more collisions.

literature.finding: Traffic on a treated street falls substantially after reallocation; pedestrian crashes scale with vehicle volume.

prediction.refute_if: Lower 95% bound above 0.65 (the predicted central fall is excluded).

discrimination.note: Power from persons injured 2014-2018 (peds_power.json); the test counts crashes, slightly fewer, so the se will be a little larger. A five-month post window (Oct 2019-Feb 2020) has a minimum detectable change of about 48% and is secondary only. Year-to-year sd of the log ratio 2013-2018 was 0.15, consistent with Poisson noise.

plan: analyses/street_space/peds_test.py and peds_common.py (committed before this registration): h9gi-nx95 crashes with a pedestrian injured or killed, located within 30 m of each corridor segment between the 9th and 3rd Avenue intersections; pre Oct 2014-Sep 2019, post Oct 2019-Sep 2022; ratio of rate ratios with Poisson interval. Rules 1, 2 and 10.
alternatives: The pandemic changed traffic and walking differently in Midtown (offices, theatres) and around 14th Street (residential, Union Square).
Other street changes on the control corridors (for example 34th Street and 42nd Street bus lanes, Open Streets).
Geocoding changes in the NYPD data over time, common to all corridors.
Pedestrian volumes on 14th Street rose after the busway, which would raise exposure and hide a fall in risk per pedestrian.
data_seen_before_registration: h9gi-nx95: pedestrian-injury crashes in the bounding box, January 2013 to 30 September 2019 (design, peds_power.json); crash locations at 9th and 3rd Avenue intersections before October 2019 (geometry). No crash after 30 September 2019 has been queried.
